name: Mazar-e-Quaid
address: Mazar-e-Quaid-e-Azam, M.A. Jinnah Road, Gurmandir, Jacob Lines, Jamshed Town, Karachi Division, Sindh 75000, Pakistan

name: Frere Hall
address: Frere Hall, Civil Lines, Saddar Town, Karachi Division, Sindh 74400, Pakistan
entryConditions: No venue-specific opening hours, entry fee or contact are published. The Sindh Tourism Development Corporation's Frere Hall page (stdc.gos.pk) and KMC's Karachi pages (kmc.gos.pk / things-to-do-in-karachi, kmc-heritage) describe the building but give no per-day timetable or ticket price; the only 'Opening Hours: Mon - Fri 9:00 am - 5:00 pm' text on kmc.gos.pk is the site-wide KMC Head Office footer, not Frere Hall's own hours. Frere Hall houses a public library; library timings circulating online (e.g. '10am-5pm Mon-Sat') appear only on social media / blogs, which are not acceptable sources, so hours stay null. The published KMC number (021-992 1511-7 / mayor@kmc.gos.pk) is the corporation's head office, not a Frere Hall line, so contact is left null to avoid misattribution.

Both the official KMC pages and the Sindh Tourism Development Corporation's Frere Hall page publish NO opening hours, entry fee or venue contact, so those fields are null rather than guessed.

name: Empress Market
address: Empress Market, Shahrah-e-Liaquat (Frere Road), Saddar Bazaar, Fowler Lines, Saddar, Karachi Division, Sindh 75530, Pakistan
entryConditions: No official opening hours, entry fee or venue contact were found. As a covered public bazaar it is generally free to enter, but no official source was found stating that explicitly, so ticketPrices is null. The only hours text is the site-wide KMC Head Office footer (Mon-Fri 9:00-5:00), which is NOT the market's opening time; the published KMC head-office number is not the market's contact, so contact is null.

Hours and ticketPrices are therefore null, not invented.

The DoAM page publishes no opening hours or entry fee, so those fields are null.

name: National Museum of Pakistan
address: Burns Garden, Dr. Zia-ud-din Ahmed Road, Karachi (per Government of Pakistan Department of Archaeology & Museums heritage-sites page); OSM places the building near Shahrah-e-Quaid area near Pakistan Secretariat, Saddar Town, 75530
entryConditions: The official federal page (Department of Archaeology & Museums, doam.gov.pk/public/heritage-sites/792) gives the museum's history and collection but publishes NO opening hours, NO entry fee, NO photography rules and NO Karachi-specific contact. A timetable reading '09AM to 05PM, except Wednesdays' circulates via the museum's Facebook page (facebook.com/NationalMuseumPK), but Facebook serves a login/JS wall and the page could not be fetched, so per the honesty rules hours remain null and that snippet is recorded only as an unverifiable secondary mention, not as data. Blog/aggregator ticket figures (e.g. PKR 20) were not used. The only phone on the DoAM page is the Department's Islamabad head office (+92 51-9252516), not the museum's line, so contact is left null.
sources: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=National+Museum+of+Pakistan+Karachi&format=jsonv2&addressdetails=1&limit=3 (supplied: osmId, lat, lng, address - same geo source as batch-b record)

description: The National Museum of Pakistan in Karachi was established on 17 April 1950 in Frere Hall, replacing the defunct Victoria Museum, and moved to its present Burns Garden building on Dr. Zia-ud-din Ahmed Road in 1970, where it now houses eleven galleries and a large archaeological and historical collection, per the Government of Pakistan Department of Archaeology & Museums (doam.gov.pk). DoAM's heritage page states no opening hours or ticket prices, and no functioning official website for the museum was found, so practical fields are null rather than guessed.

name: Karachi Zoo
address: Karachi Zoo, D'Silva Street, Madina Colony, Garden West, Karachi District, Sindh 74550, Pakistan (per OpenStreetMap/Nominatim; OSM addr:street tags 'Manghopir Rd;Garden Lane'); commonly known as Garden Zoo, Garden East
entryConditions: No official zoo timetable or tariff page could be read: the managing body's own KMC page (kmc.gos.pk/karachi-zoo/) states the zoo 'covers an area of 33 acres' but publishes no opening hours or entry fee, and the Sindh Wildlife Department (swildlife.gov.pk) and City Government Karachi (thecity.gov.pk) sites were unreachable from this network (HTTP 000). The only 'Opening Hours: Mon-Fri 9:00-5:00' on kmc.gos.pk is the site-wide KMC Head Office footer, not the zoo's hours. Reputable PRESS coverage (Geo.tv, 29 December 2025) reports that Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab announced entry fees of Rs 50 (adults) / Rs 30 (children) at the 28 December 2025 reopening of upgraded facilities (new lion enclosure, renovated Reptile House); this is a press-reported figure, not an official published tariff, so it is recorded as SECONDARY and not placed in ticketPrices. Third-party listings variously claim daily opening and that Wednesdays are reserved for women and children - unverified and not used. Do not present the zoo as definitively open or closed.

description: Karachi Zoo (Karachi Zoological and Botanical Gardens, also called Garden Zoo) in Garden East is a historic zoo - KMC's own page notes it was established in 1878 and covers an area of 33 acres, and OpenStreetMap records its operator as the Sindh Government. No official page publishes its opening hours or entry fee (KMC's zoo page is silent; swildlife.gov.pk and thecity.gov.pk were unreachable), so hours and ticketPrices are null; press coverage (Geo.tv, Dec 2025) reported Mayor-announced fees of Rs 50 / Rs 30, recorded only as secondary.

name: Chaukhandi Tombs
address: Chaukhandi Tombs, Chowkhandi Road, Abdullah Goth, Bin Qasim Town, Malir District, Karachi Division, Sindh 75030, Pakistan (per OpenStreetMap/Nominatim; UNESCO describes it as '40 km east of Karachi')
entryConditions: No official published opening hours, entry fee or contact were found. The necropolis is inscribed on Pakistan's UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List (Ref. 1287, submitted 14/12/1993) and is conserved/managed by the Sindh Culture, Tourism & Antiquities Department (Government of Sindh), which posts guided tourist visits via its official Facebook page (facebook.com/AntiquitieSindh) - a login-walled page that could not be fetched here. It is an active Muslim graveyard as well as a heritage site (OSM amenity=grave_yard, religion=muslim), so respectful visiting is implied but no official rules page exists. Visit-time figures circulating online (e.g. '07:00-19:00') and the 'no official entrance fee, tip the caretaker' note come only from Google/Tripadvisor-style aggregators and travel blogs, which are not acceptable sources, so hours and ticketPrices are null and no fee figure is published.
sources: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=Chaukhandi+Tombs+Karachi&format=jsonv2&addressdetails=1&limit=3 (supplied: osmId, lat, lng, address - same geo source as batch-d record)

description: The Chaukhandi necropolis, about 40 km east of Karachi, is a funerary ensemble of elaborately carved stone warriors' tombs, inscribed on Pakistan's UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List (Ref. 1287, submitted 14 December 1993) and conserved by the Sindh Culture, Tourism & Antiquities Department of the Government of Sindh. No official source publishes opening hours, an entry fee or a contact number, so those fields are null; the site is also an active Muslim graveyard.
